title: Threshold Guardrail Runway & Owner Slate
body:
Purpose:
This doc is a compact operational runway for the upcoming feature launch. It focuses on: 1) quantitative guardrails (green/amber/red), 2) KPI baselines and targets, 3) escalation and immediate contingency actions, and 4) clear owner map for each signal. Treat as the single source-of-truth for launch day decision-making until the postmortem is published.

Scope and audience:
- Scope: Beta -> 100% ramp across hosted API and Dedicated customers (soft-launch cohort then broader ramp).
- Audience: Product Ops, Release Eng, SRE, Observability, Solutions Eng, Customer Success, GTM PMs.

Quick summary (one-liners):
- Canary window: 48 hours with progressive ramp (5% -> 20% -> 50% -> 100%) if guardrails hold.
- Primary KPIs to watch: Activation rate, 95p latency, error rate (5xx), token cost/unit, and quality regressions on eval test set.
- Critical kill criteria: sustained 95p latency > 1.5x target for 30m without improved trend OR error rate > 3% for 15m.

Baseline KPIs (pre-launch week average):
- Activation rate (new users exposed -> feature-enabled): 6.1%
- 95th percentile latency (hosted API, prime path): 320ms
- Aggregate 5xx error rate: 0.4%
- Token cost per active session (median): $0.011
- Quality match on eval set (weighted F1 / baseline model): 0.94

Target thresholds for rollout gating (green / amber / red):
- Activation rate: green = >= 5% (OK), amber = 3-5% (investigate UX), red = <3% (pause ramp).
- 95p latency: green = <= 400ms, amber = 400-700ms, red = >700ms OR 1.5x baseline for 30m.
- 5xx error rate: green = <= 1.0%, amber = 1.0-2.5%, red = >2.5% sustained 15m.
- Token cost: green = within +10% of baseline, amber = +10-25% (cost review), red = >+25% (hold and analyze batching/quant settings).
- Quality on eval set: green >= 0.92, amber 0.88-0.92 (A/B validate on subset), red <0.88 (rollback to previous model variant).

Traffic ramp schedule (recommended):
- Canary phase (Day 0-2): 5% traffic for 6 hours -> assess signals -> optionally hold 12 hours -> if stable, 20% for 12 hours -> assess -> 50% for 12 hours -> full.
- Week 1 post-launch: staged increases only during weekday business hours, with no more than 2x day-over-day increase after Day 2.

Measurement windows and dashboards (where to look):
- Short windows (1m/5m): latency, error rate, CPU/GPU utilization on serving clusters (Dashboards: ReleaseOps/Canary-Short).
- Medium windows (15m/1h): trending on activation and retention events, user-level errors (Dashboards: ReleaseOps/Canary-Trend).
- Long windows (24h): cost per token, session token distribution, qualitative eval samples (Dashboards: Product-KPI/Launch-24h).

Decision owners (who calls green/hold/rollback):
- Safety/Model quality: Samir Patel (Applied ML) — authority to rollback model variant.
- Runtime & infra (latency, errors): Priya Singh (Site Reliability) — authority to pause ramp and trigger infra failover.
- Product adoption (activation, UX blocking): Marco Reyes (Product Growth) — can request hold for UX issues.
- Cost & billing: Tina Li (Finance Ops) — can pause broad rollout if cost exceeds red threshold.
- Final go/no-go during canary: Asha Kapoor (Product Ops) — coordinates cross-team decision and communicates externally.

Contingency matrix (failure mode -> immediate action -> owner -> notes):
- High 95p latency spike (red): scale up serving pool (auto or manual), enable temporary traffic-throttle to Dedicated-only, roll back heavy quant/kv-cache changes. Owner: Priya Singh. Notes: start 15m timer; if not resolving in 30m, revert to previous runtime config.
- Increased 5xx errors: switch to fallback model variant (compat model with smaller context), open P0 incident, reduce canary to 0% if errors affect >2% traffic. Owner: Priya Singh + Samir Patel.
- Quality regression on eval set / user complaints: pause ramp, route new sessions to previous model variant, run prioritized eval harness. Owner: Samir Patel. Notes: hold until A/B confidence confirms improvement.
- Unexpected cost growth: enable cost-gating rule (throttle lower-tier traffic), pause non-essential batch jobs, and assess batching/quantization. Owner: Tina Li.
- UX blocking bug (activation funnel): rollback UI flag or disable feature gate for cohort. Owner: Marco Reyes.

Acceptance checklist (must be green unless explicitly overridden):
- [ ] Canary automation configured (ramp script + rollback API).
- [ ] Dashboards created and validated: ReleaseOps/Canary-Short, Canary-Trend, Product-KPI/Launch-24h.
- [ ] Alert thresholds (pager and Slack) set for latency and error rate.
- [ ] Canary cohort list finalized and feature gates in place.
- [ ] Observability hooks for token-level cost and per-route traces enabled.
- [ ] Runbook drafted and shared with SRE on-call rotation.
- [ ] Post-launch eval set and sampling method defined (owner: Samir).
- [ ] Customer success notified of beta cohort and escalation path.

Rapid playbook (first 30 minutes if red condition observed):
1) Post incident note in channel #launch-ops with title and top-3 signals.
2) Triage owner acknowledges and assigns immediate tasks.
3) If latency or errors: reduce canary to 0% or route traffic to last-known-good variant.
4) Collect minimal repro and top traces; capture recent deploy list.
5) If quality: mark suspected model, snapshot request logs, sink failing examples to secure bucket.

Runbook snippets (copy for on-call to paste):
- Pause ramp: POST /release-control/v1/ramp -d '{"action":"pause","id":"feature-x"}' (ops-only key).
- Rollback model: POST /models/v1/serve -d '{"action":"switch","model":"feature-x-v0.9"}' (applied-ml key).
- Enable throttling: scripts/traffic/throttle.sh --percent 30 --route /api/v1/generate

Risk register (top open risks and mitigations):
- Risk: Spike due to cold start for edge regions. Mitigation: pre-warm nodes, set conservative canary in those regions. Owner: Release Eng.
- Risk: Cost mis-estimate for long tail sessions. Mitigation: cap per-session token limit for first 72 hours and monitor per-user spend. Owner: Finance Ops.
- Risk: Data privacy audit delay for private deployment customers. Mitigation: delay inclusion of private-deploy cohort until sign-off. Owner: Legal & Compliance.

Sign-off table (names and sign-off window):
- Product Manager (feature): Elena Park — sign-off by D-1 17:00 PT
- Release Engineering: Carlos Vega — sign-off by D-1 18:00 PT
- SRE: Priya Singh — sign-off by D-1 18:30 PT
- Applied ML: Samir Patel — sign-off by D-1 16:30 PT
- Customer Success: Jenna Ortiz — informed by D-1 12:00 PT
- Finance: Tina Li — informed by D-2 for cost gating limits

Notes and open questions (working list):
- Can we set a soft cap on overall token spend for the canary cohort? (Action: Tina to confirm limits and config point.)
- Are any customers in Dedicated likely to fail over during the canary window? (Action: Solutions Eng to validate Dedicated isolation.)
- Evaluate possibility of pre-baked fallback prompts to reduce hallucination during initial rollout. (Action: Samir to prototype.)

Post-launch operations (first 72 hours):
- Daily 09:30 sync for first 3 days with SRE/Product/Samr, 30m standup to escalate unresolved issues.
- At 24h: publish preliminary kpi snapshot and incident log.
- At 72h: run small A/B evaluation against baseline model on held-out dataset and decide on broad rollout.

Appendix: quick links and scripts
- Canary ramp script: internal repo: https://github.com/redwood/release-tools/tree/main/canary-ramp
- Runtime config snapshot: s3://redwood-configs/releases/feature-x/2025-01-08

Document history:
- 2025-01-09: initial draft by Asha Kapoor
- 2025-01-21: added contingency matrix and owners (collaborators: Marco, Samir)
- 2025-02-14: updated thresholds after load test; ready for review

End of doc.
